status: Frozen documentary inputs; subsequent corrections require an amendment

observations.observation: Fish is reared through containers to sea; announces a relative year; ship is tied to fishhorn and then a tree at northern mountain; Manu survives/descent follows recession.
observations.interpretive_limit: Relative prediction has no independent calendar. Geographical identification of mountain needs evidence outside this wording.
observations.bounded_absence: Passage1–6 supplies no historical king list, dated deposition layer or unique Harappan locality; later translator footnote references are outside this passage.

dating.narrated_time: relative such-and-such year and recession sequence

observations.observation: Offered dairy produces daughter; she authorizes her use in the middle of sacrifice; passage identifies her with Iḍā and extends Manu's successful offspring/cattle to the current performer.
observations.interpretive_limit: The text binds a present rite to an ancestral precedent. It does not date first adoption of dairy offerings.

observations.observation: Five-part portions, handing to Hotṛ, ghee/lip actions and paired breathing formulas, protective low voice, Vedastudy/teaching and five eaters form specific instructions around an origin story.
observations.interpretive_limit: Operational detail is genuinely explicit. Its continuous performance from Harappa is a separate, unestablished route.

observations.observation: River/goddess praise includes strength, protection, mountain/samudra wording and gift to Nahuṣa. Conventional Griffith translation gives mountains-to-ocean.
observations.interpretive_limit: Poetic protection and nourishment cannot independently identify urban architecture or a hydrological discharge class.
observations.bounded_absence: The inspected verses state no calendar or diagnostic depositional change.

dating.narrated_time: praise and attributed gift, not an annal

observations.observation: Thomson challenges the conventional direction through the ablative form samudrāt and its parallels. Conventional rendering and challenge are both retained.
observations.interpretive_limit: We did not adjudicate this linguistic dispute; neither branch licenses a calendar join to sampled river sediments.

observations.observation: Named river invocation includes Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Paruṣṇī and others; surrounding hymn centers Sindhu.
observations.interpretive_limit: Names and regional configuration offer more external testing opportunities than a general flood. Which name denotes which reach at composition remains an identification question.
observations.bounded_absence: The list itself gives no river abandonment date.

observations.observation: Discourse answers inherited superiority claims and explains mixed good/bad conduct across four classes; origin narrative occurs in recurring cosmic expansion with luminous beings.
observations.interpretive_limit: The account explicitly serves ethical status and cosmological explanation; a historical chronicle reading requires separate support.

observations.observation: Rice collection is enlarged to multiple days; hoarding changes magically regenerative rice; beings divide rice and establish boundaries; repeated taking others' shares prompts reprimand and violence.
observations.interpretive_limit: The property/theft dependency is explicit. The disappearance of effortless rice is a moral/cosmic causal claim rather than measured agriculture.

observations.observation: Community selects an attractive illustrious being to censure and expel appropriately, paying a rice share; Mahāsammata, khattiya and rājā receive explanatory derivations.
observations.interpretive_limit: Role and compensation relations are concrete; the passage does not authenticate elected Harappan kings or taxation.
observations.bounded_absence: No Harappan personal name, place, administrative sign or calendar occurs in these inspected paragraphs.

observations.observation: Divine warning concerns lethal winter and deep snow; preservation uses an enclosure containing selected people, animals and plant seeds, water and dwelling arrangements.
observations.interpretive_limit: Rescue/world renewal template overlaps broadly with Manu but agents, hazard and preservation device differ. Shared ancestry, diffusion and separate construction remain alternatives.
observations.bounded_absence: The inspected primary paragraphs do not describe Manu's fish towing a ship; translator's Noah comparison is commentary.

observations.locus: Chronology of palaeochannel fluvial sands; Regional analysis; Discussion
observations.observation: Main paper derives52OSLburialages from7cores; Kalibangan transect large-river deposits ceased betweenabout23and12.3ka, regional late activity inMNK6endsabout8ka; provenance supports former Sutlejcourse.
observations.interpretive_limit: These are measured stratigraphic/process/provenance claims for sampled locations, not dates of a named poem.

dating.system: source kaBP; BP not converted to BCE
dating.provenance: U-Pbzircon and Ar-Armica Maages identify source rocks, not sediment burial or hymn composition

observations.observation: SRTMmorphology plus AMSradiocarbon/OSL of deposits underpin claim against large glacier-fed HoloceneGhaggar-Hakra. Authors allow active monsoon-fed rivers with possible perennial groundwaterbaseflow; dated deposits differ by reach.
observations.interpretive_limit: Absence of glacier supply is not absence of all water or year-roundflow. Sample age is not the age of a river name.

observations.locus: Stratigraphy; The evolving river system; Methodology; Fig1–3
observations.observation: About300km basin synthesis combines shell AMSradiocarbon/quartzOSL with detritalmica and Sr-Ndprovenance; authors infer renewed Himalayan supply/perennialflow9–4.5ka through Sutlejdistributaries.
observations.interpretive_limit: The inferred year-roundwater model and Sarasvatī identification extend sediment/provenance evidence. Main channel abandonment and temporary distributary supply require reach-matched tests.

observations.observation: ChautangnearHissar stratifiedquartzOSL study reports cessation of a major Himalayanfluvial system well beforeHarappa and criticizes direct settlement-number/river-strength inference.
observations.interpretive_limit: Only abstract accessed; no numerical age extracted. Chautang reach does not automatically adjudicate everyGhaggar deposit.

observations.observation: Indexed author excerpt qualifies very stable Vedic transmission as strictly applicable after collection/redaction, while arguing earlier changes minimal.
observations.interpretive_limit: Exactness after a corpus is fixed does not independently establish its precollection story age.

observations.observation: In25contemporaryMaharashtraschools, observed lessons fragment and string text, revision corrects pronunciation/intonation, advancedstudents sometimes guide revision, printedbooks aid earlylearning.
observations.interpretive_limit: A measured present mechanism can motivate historical hypotheses; sample is not statistically representative and does not observe each ancient transmission interval.

observations.observation: Allon argues early sutras were fixed for communal memorization yet communities sanctioned revisions; parallels differ in names, events, lists, wording and plot; a developedGandhari narrative has a2cCEmanuscript witness.
observations.interpretive_limit: Narrative elaboration can precede a later simpler surviving version. This example concerns another discourse and cannot become a DN27manuscriptdate.
